summary: This sermon examines John 6 (feeding the 5,000 and walking on water) showing how Jesus intentionally parallels the Moses/Exodus narrative to reveal He is the prophet greater than Moses promised in Deuteronomy 18. Every detail—crossing water, crowds following signs, ascending a mountain, testing disciples, Passover timing, multiplying bread—echoes the wilderness story to demonstrate Jesus is equal with God and the ultimate mediator surpassing Moses.
key_points: Jesus structures the feeding miracle to deliberately mirror Moses and the Exodus story in every detail
Jesus demonstrates superiority over Moses: better location, better provision, walking on water rather than through it
God's tests reveal what we truly believe about Him and invite deeper relationship, not to make us fail
The crowd recognizes Jesus as the prophet but wants to force Him to be their political deliverer—right answer, wrong application
Jesus withdraws from those seeking to use Him for their agenda but draws near to disciples willing to submit
big_idea: Jesus is not always the king we want (fixing our temporary earthly problems) but exactly the king we need (restoring us to the Father and giving eternal hope beyond our circumstances).
title: Like No Other: Feeding Five Thousand & Walking on Water!
